memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "(The flax and barley were destroyed, since the barley had headed and the flax was in bloom. The wheat and spelt, however, were not destroyed, because they ripen later.)" - Exodus 9:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This little note in brackets is easy to skip. It tells us which crops were destroyed and which survived, based on where they were in the growing season.

Two things are worth seeing here.

First, this is history, not legend. The writer knows Egyptian agriculture and gives us the kind of detail that only someone familiar with the land would include. Our faith rests on events that happened in real places, at real times, with real harvests.

Second, and more sobering: the wheat and spelt survived. And that is exactly what the locusts would eat in the next chapter. What Pharaoh had left to hold on to, he would soon lose too.

Partial obedience leaves us with something still to lose. God, in mercy, kept dismantling every remaining foundation until Pharaoh had nothing to trust in but God Himself. Sadly, Pharaoh never took the step.

Sometimes God removes our reserves not to impoverish us but to bring us to the end of our self-reliance, where real faith begins.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What am I still holding as my back-up plan instead of trusting God?
2. Do I believe God can be trusted when my reserves are gone?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You know what I am still quietly relying on. Loosen my grip and teach me to trust You completely. Amen.
